summary: The Strengthening Essential Manufacturing and Industrial Investment Act, or the SEMI Investment Act, amends the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to extend and expand the advanced manufacturing investment credit. It broadens the definition of an advanced manufacturing facility to include the manufacturing of semiconductors, semiconductor manufacturing equipment, and specific semiconductor materials, while also extending the expiration date for the credit period.

affected_groups.effect: Eligible to claim the advanced manufacturing investment credit for facilities producing semiconductors, equipment, and a wider range of direct and indirect production materials, and through an extended timeframe until December 31, 2031.
affected_groups.group: Taxpayers and manufacturers in the semiconductor industry

affected_groups.effect: Required to consult with one another to publish and maintain annual lists of qualifying semiconductor materials and to review taxpayer petitions for interim material determinations.
affected_groups.group: Federal agencies (Department of the Treasury and Department of Commerce)

key_provisions: Expands the definition of an advanced manufacturing facility to include facilities whose primary purpose is manufacturing semiconductors, semiconductor manufacturing equipment, or semiconductor materials.

Includes direct production materials (such as substrates, thin films, packaging substrates, and bonding or adhesive materials) that are primarily used for and integral to semiconductor production and physically incorporated into the finished semiconductor.

Includes indirect production materials (such as process chemicals, photolithography materials, cleaning agents, and testing materials) that are specialized and used in semiconductor manufacturing without being physically incorporated into the final product.
Excludes from the definition of indirect production materials any items that have generic uses or are predominantly used in applications other than semiconductor manufacturing.

Requires the Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of Commerce, to publish an official list of qualifying direct and indirect semiconductor materials within 180 days of enactment and annually thereafter, and allows taxpayers to petition for interim determinations.
Extends the credit period by changing the expiration date for property construction beginning from December 31, 2026, to December 31, 2031.
